taskSummary: Fix LaTeX printer dropping the separator between multi-part symbol subscripts

steps.label: failure
steps.title: run the failing scoped test
steps.text:
$ python -m pytest sympy/printing/tests/test_latex.py -k test_latex_symbols -q

F                                                                        [100%]
================================== FAILURES ==================================
_____________________________ test_latex_symbols ______________________________

    def test_latex_symbols():
        ...
>       assert latex(Symbol('x_i_j')) == 'x_{i j}'
E       AssertionError: assert 'x_{ij}' == 'x_{i j}'
E         - x_{i j}
E         + x_{ij}

sympy/printing/tests/test_latex.py:842: AssertionError
1 failed, 1 passed in 0.42s

steps.label: note
steps.title: diagnose the failure
steps.text: Symbol('x_i_j') represents x with two separate subscript indices, i and j, rendered as x_{i j} — a space-separated brace group that reads unambiguously as two indices rather than one two-character subscript. _print_Symbol builds this by joining the parts split_super_sub extracts from the symbol's name; the subscript branch was joining with an empty separator, collapsing ['i', 'j'] into the ambiguous x_{ij}.

steps.label: fix
steps.title: join subscript parts with a space, matching the superscript branch
steps.text: Join multiple subscript parts with a literal space before wrapping them in braces, the same convention the superscript branch two lines below already uses: ' '.join(subs) instead of ''.join(subs).

steps.label: diff
steps.title: the fix
steps.text:
--- a/sympy/printing/latex.py
+++ b/sympy/printing/latex.py
@@ def _print_Symbol(self, expr, style='plain'):
     name, supers, subs = split_super_sub(expr.name)
     name = translate(name)
     supers = [translate(sup) for sup in supers]
     subs = [translate(sub) for sub in subs]
 
     if subs:
-        name += '_{%s}' % ''.join(subs)
+        name += '_{%s}' % ' '.join(subs)
     if supers:
         name += '^{%s}' % ' '.join(supers)
 
     return name

steps.label: command
steps.title: rerun — passing
steps.text:
$ python -m pytest sympy/printing/tests/test_latex.py -k test_latex_symbols -q

.                                                                        [100%]
1 passed in 0.31s

synthesis: sympy's LaTeX printer represents a symbol like Symbol('x_i_j') as two separate subscript indices, i and j, rendered as x_{i j} — a space-separated brace group that reads unambiguously as two indices rather than one two-character subscript. _print_Symbol builds this by joining the parts split_super_sub extracts from the symbol's name, and the subscript branch had regressed to an empty-string join, collapsing ['i', 'j'] into the ambiguous x_{ij}. The superscript branch a few lines below already joined with a space, so the fix makes the subscript branch consistent with it. The regression test test_latex_symbols pins the exact rendered string for a two-part subscript symbol, so this class of join-separator bug cannot reappear silently.
